searchText: <@387536747476549632> commit a hash of a thing in one bl,ck, then wait a while, then reveal what you previously committed. The hash is unique to you, and the front runner doesn't know the answer, and they cannot do the action without revealing in advance. <@!301186049323958275> seems like a beautiful solution. how come contracts haven't implemented this? Is it because contract needing to hash data is gas costly? <@387536747476549632> requires multiple transactions separated by time. Poor UX for regular users. are there any EIPS proposed around this? No need for an EIP. ENS uses this strategy to prevent front-running of name purchases. You commit a hash of the name you want, then wait a couple minutes, then execute the purchase of the name. Thee name isn't revealed to the network until the second transaction, and by then it is too late for a front-runner to steal the name from you. interesting. reading up on this. thanks.
